newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber prices close with extended losses.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber prices close with extended losses.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices extended their losses at the close as there was no sign of buyers returning to the market, dealers said.
A weaker Tokyo market also pulled down prices, they said.
"There's still no sign of overseas buyers. They are probably buying rubber of other origin," said one local dealer.
Dealers said consumers were also discouraged by a strong ringgit against the U.S. dollar.
Ample supply of raw materials, due to a recent turnaround in the weather, was putting pressure on prices, they added.

At the close, February RSS1 buyer was quoted at 306.50 cents ($1.23) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, down three cents from Thursday. February SMR 20 buyer was down 1.50 cents at 304 cents a kg.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 306 cents a kg, SMR CV at 369, SMR L at 351, SMR 5 at 317, SMR 10 at 307 and drum latex FOB at 240.
The INRO five-day moving average was 239.90 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Jan 9 against 240.68 on Jan 8. The daily indicator price was 238.24 versus 238.79.
